# RETRO: PR #13064

## What worked
- Executed verbatim-extraction harness (Opus) settled handler order and delegate teardown timing that source reading alone got wrong once (Sol's deferred-deletion assumption).
- Neutral cross-examination converged both reviewers: Sol independently found the kinds-conversion root cause when pointed at the model-boundary source area, and withdrew two claims after tracing the teardown chain itself.
- The mid-run third-party comment was already covered by an in-flight follow-up; a guard variant was added to that follow-up at no extra round.

## Avoidable friction / process deviations
- Coordinator: two 50-line workflow chunks read in parallel in one response (aggregate over 60 lines).
- Coordinator: comment-requirements.md lines 46-95 first read through a 160-character width projection (awk substr); re-read fully before drafting.
- Opus reviewer (self-reported): host-side `python3` twice outside review.py (reading intake JSON; editing its own fixture), host `sed` to derive run-f2.sh/run-f4.sh from existing fixtures, and a few 51-54 line source reads. No pinned-source or outside-assignment writes reported. None of these affects the public claims (the fixture edits are text edits of reviewer-owned files; execution evidence is from sealed review.py runs).
- The fixed Opus launch prompt cannot carry first-call rules; they were placed at the top of a 34-line brief so the first read stays within bounds. Suggest the omarchy-reviewer agent definition repeat the metadata and 60-line rules itself.

## Improvements
- comment-requirements.md "Current model preference" still says "New reviews use Opus 5.5 High"; update to the effort policy (xhigh default) so snapshots do not need an applicability override.
- Brief template could prompt reviewers to check data crossing QML model boundaries (Instantiator/Repeater) when a PR relies on manifest-derived checks.

## Tool notes
- No Omadev use. review.py worked for offscreen qml6 harnesses once stderr was forced to a file (Opus review2 failure: Qt logging went to journald when stderr was not a TTY).

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the empty app grid is real, and in an isolated harness on this head `refreshPanelPluginApis()` gives a loaded third-party menu panel a working `shell.appLibrary` again at the next `prunePluginApis()`. The underlying cause, however, is at panel load rather than in the prune, so the refresh repairs the panel only after the fact and some paths stay broken. The refresh also runs for plugins that were just disabled.

### A third-party menu panel receives a facade without `appLibrary` at load

`onLoaded` builds the scoped shell from `panelEntry.manifest`, which has passed through the panel `Instantiator` model. Qt converts `kinds` into a sequence type on the way, so `Array.isArray(kinds)` is false and `manifestHasKind(manifest, "menu")` returns false.

```text
registry manifest       kinds: ["menu"]          real JS Array
  -> computePanelEntries -> Instantiator model    (converted to QVariantList)
  -> panelEntry.manifest  kinds: sequence object   Array.isArray(kinds) === false
  -> onLoaded: pluginShellFor(panelEntry.manifest)
       profile own-service|no-bar|no-menu, appLibrary: null   <- grid empty from load
next prunePluginApis(): expects own-service|no-bar|menu (from the registry manifest)
  base: revoke -> panel keeps shell === null, nothing re-delivers it
  head: revoke -> refresh from installedPlugins[id] -> appLibrary present
```

The table summarizes an isolated harness that runs the functions, `Connections`, `Instantiator` and `Loader` copied verbatim from each pinned `shell/shell.qml` on Qt 6.11.2 (registry, app library and services stubbed):

| Scenario (synthetic harness) | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Menu panel just loaded | `appLibrary` null | `appLibrary` null |
| After the next prune | `shell` null | `appLibrary` present |
| Panel recreated (any panel, overlay or menu plugin enabled or disabled), before another prune | `appLibrary` null | `appLibrary` null |
| Another holder requests the facade with the registry manifest (the call `Bar.qml` makes via `pluginShellForId`) | `shell` null | `shell` null, later prunes do not repair it |

**Impact:** every load or reload of a third-party `menu` panel (and a `bar`-kind panel) starts without `appLibrary`, on this PR as on base. It recovers only if a later prune happens, which depends on event timing.

**Suggested change:** build the panel facade from the registry manifest in `onLoaded`, for example `shell.pluginShellFor(shell.pluginRegistry.installedPlugins[panelEntry.pluginId] || panelEntry.manifest)`, or make `manifestHasKind()` accept array-like `kinds`. In the harness, the `onLoaded` change alone, without the refresh, kept `appLibrary` present across load, reload, prune, second-holder, disable/re-enable and kinds-change scenarios.

### Revokes inside `createScopedPluginShell()` are not re-delivered

`createScopedPluginShell()` revokes a cached facade whenever a caller asks for a different profile (`shell/shell.qml`, around lines 566-570). The panel asks with the converted manifest (`no-menu`); `pluginShellForId()` from `Bar.qml`, the kept-service path in `_syncServices()` and `ensureService()` ask with the registry manifest (`menu`). The new refresh is only called from the prune.

**Impact:** a plugin with a panel and a second holder, such as a menu plus bar widget (the same kinds as the built-in `omarchy.menu`), can leave its panel with `shell === null`. Later prunes do not revoke again because the cached profile now matches, so the panel stays broken. In the other direction, a panel reload can revoke the facade the bar widget or service holds (from source reading, not run).

**Suggested change:** the `onLoaded` change above removes the profile disagreement. In the harness, the panel and the bar-shaped caller then shared one facade instead of revoking each other's.

### The refresh also runs for disabled plugins

The refresh is called after every revoke, including `!active`, and `refreshPanelPluginApis()` only returns early when the plugin is missing from `installedPlugins`. Disabled plugins stay in `installedPlugins`. On `pluginsChanged`, bar-widget re-registration emits `barWidgetRegistry.changed` and prunes before the panel handler removes the panel, so the refresh builds new facades for the just-disabled plugin and hands them to the panel that is about to be destroyed. In the harness this happened on every disable of a live panel on this PR (never on base), for `menu`, `panel` and `overlay` plugins.

**Impact:** with Qt 6.11.2's current handler order, the final prune of the same event revokes these facades, and nothing stale remained in the harness after disable or on re-enable. That clean end state relies on the order in which several `Connections` blocks on `pluginsChanged` run, which Qt does not document. With that order changed synthetically in the harness, a re-enabled panel reused a leftover facade whose `bar` (and, for menus, `appLibrary`) pointed at deleted objects.

**Suggested change:** only refresh when the plugin is active, for example `if (active && descriptor) shell.refreshPanelPluginApis(String(descriptor.pluginId || ""))`. In the harness this variant created no facades for disabled plugins under either handler order and kept the repair in the profile-mismatch scenarios.

**Description accuracy:** `revokePluginShellApi()` destroys the scoped `shell` and its app-library proxy, not all four properties: `manifest`, `pluginRegistry` and `barWidgetRegistry` remain valid. Disabled plugins are not skipped by the `installedPlugins` lookup, as the description states; their panels are torn down before the last prune by handler order.

**Verified:** no regression found for built-in panels (first-party manifests get the host shell), closed non-kept panels (no item, so the refresh returns), or removed plugins. The existing static check in `test/shell.d/plugin-auth-boundary-test.sh` still matches the edited prune branch (checked by reading).

**Optional test improvement:** a runtime check that `item.shell.appLibrary` is non-null immediately after a third-party menu panel's `onLoaded`, before any further registry or bar-widget signal, fails on both base and this head in the harness, so it would cover the load-time cause that this PR leaves open.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of `shell/shell.qml`, the plugin registry and API services, `Bar.qml` and `Menu.qml` at the pinned head and base, plus Qt Declarative 6.11.2 source for the model conversion, delegate teardown and handler ordering. Behavior was checked in an isolated QML harness (Qt 6.11.2, offscreen) built from functions copied verbatim out of the pinned `shell/shell.qml`, with the registry, app library and services stubbed. The Quickshell runtime, the real `Bar.qml` and services, a live desktop session and Qt versions before 6.11.2 were not exercised. The specific revoke behind the reported clean-login symptom was not traced in a running shell.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
